sentences.en: Translator: Joseph Geni Reviewer: Morton Bast When I was in my 20s,
sentences.zh: 译者：Joseph Geni 审稿人：Morton Bast 当我20多岁的时候，

sentences.en: I saw my very first psychotherapy client.
sentences.zh: 我见到了我的第一个心理治疗客户。

sentences.en: I was a Ph.D. student in clinical psychology at Berkeley.
sentences.zh: 我是一名博士。伯克利临床心理学学生。

sentences.en: She was a 26-year-old woman named Alex. Now Alex walked into her first session wearing jeans and a big slouchy top, and she dropped onto the couch in my office and kicked off her flats
sentences.zh: 她是一位名叫亚历克斯的 26 岁女性。现在，亚历克斯穿着牛仔裤和宽松的大上衣走进了她的第一次治疗，她坐在我办公室的沙发上，踢掉了她的平底鞋

sentences.en: and told me she was there to talk about guy problems.
sentences.zh: 并告诉我她来这里是为了谈论男人的问题。

sentences.en: Now when I heard this, I was so relieved.
sentences.zh: 现在听到这句话，我心里顿时松了口气。

sentences.en: My classmate got an arsonist for her first client.
sentences.zh: 我的同学为她的第一个客户找到了纵火犯。

sentences.en: (Laughter) And I got a twentysomething who wanted to talk about boys.
sentences.zh: （笑声） 我遇到了一个二十多岁的人，他想谈论男孩。

sentences.en: This I thought I could handle. But I didn't handle it.
sentences.zh: 我以为我可以处理这个问题。但我没处理好。

sentences.en: With the funny stories that Alex would bring to session, it was easy for me just to nod my head while we kicked the can down the road.
sentences.zh: 亚历克斯会在会议上带来有趣的故事，当我们把罐子踢到路上时，我很容易点头。

sentences.en: "Thirty's the new 20," Alex would say, and as far as I could tell, she was right.
sentences.zh: “三十是新的二十，”亚历克斯会说，据我所知，她是对的。

sentences.en: Work happened later, marriage happened later, kids happened later, even death happened later.
sentences.zh: 工作发生得晚一些，婚姻发生得晚一些，孩子发生得晚一些，甚至死亡发生得晚一些。

sentences.en: Twentysomethings like Alex and I had nothing but time.
sentences.zh: 像亚历克斯和我这样二十多岁的人除了时间之外一无所有。

sentences.en: But before long, my supervisor pushed me to push Alex about her love life.
sentences.zh: 但不久之后，我的主管催促我向亚历克斯推销她的爱情生活。

sentences.en: I pushed back. I said, "Sure, she's dating down, she's sleeping with a knucklehead, but it's not like she's going to marry the guy."
sentences.zh: 我退缩了。我说：“当然，她正在约会，她正在和傻瓜睡觉，但她不会嫁给那个男人。”

sentences.en: And then my supervisor said, "Not yet, but she might marry the next one.
sentences.zh: 然后我的主管说：“还没有，但她可能会嫁给下一个。

sentences.en: Besides, the best time to work on Alex's marriage is before she has one."
sentences.zh: 此外，处理亚历克斯婚姻的最佳时机是在她结婚之前。”

sentences.en: That's what psychologists call an "Aha!" moment.
sentences.zh: 这就是心理学家所说的“啊哈！”片刻。

sentences.en: That was the moment I realized, 30 is not the new 20.
sentences.zh: 那一刻我意识到，30 岁并不是新的 20 岁。

sentences.en: Yes, people settle down later than they used to, but that didn't make Alex's 20s a developmental downtime.
sentences.zh: 是的，人们安定下来的时间比以前晚了，但这并没有让亚历克斯的 20 多岁成为发育停滞期。

sentences.en: That made Alex's 20s a developmental sweet spot, and we were sitting there, blowing it.
sentences.zh: 这让 Alex 的 20 多岁成为了发展的最佳时期，而我们却坐在那里，搞砸了。

sentences.en: That was when I realized that this sort of benign neglect was a real problem, and it had real consequences, not just for Alex and her love life but for the careers and the families and the futures
sentences.zh: 就在那时，我意识到这种良性的忽视是一个真正的问题，它产生了真正的后果，不仅对亚历克斯和她的爱情生活，而且对事业、家庭和未来

sentences.en: of twentysomethings everywhere. There are 50 million twentysomethings in the United States right now.
sentences.zh: 到处都是二十多岁的人。目前美国有 5000 万二十多岁的年轻人。

sentences.en: We're talking about 15 percent of the population, or 100 percent if you consider that no one's getting through adulthood without going through their 20s first.
sentences.zh: 我们谈论的是 15% 的人口，或者说 100%，如果你认为没有人不先经历 20 岁就度过了成年期。

sentences.en: (Laughter) Raise your hand if you're in your 20s.
sentences.zh: （笑声）如果你20多岁，请举手。

sentences.en: I really want to see some twentysomethings here.
sentences.zh: 我真的很想在这里见到一些二十多岁的人。

sentences.en: Oh, yay! You are all awesome. If you work with twentysomethings, you love a twentysomething, you're losing sleep over twentysomethings, I want to see — Okay. Awesome, twentysomethings really matter.
sentences.zh: 哦，耶！你们都很棒。如果你和二十多岁的人一起工作，你爱一个二十多岁的人，你会因为二十多岁的人而失眠，我想看看——好吧。太棒了，二十几岁真的很重要。

sentences.en: So, I specialize in twentysomethings because I believe that every single one of those 50 million twentysomethings deserves to know what psychologists, sociologists, neurologists and fertility specialists
sentences.zh: 所以，我专注于二十多岁的人，因为我相信这 5000 万二十多岁的人中的每一个都应该了解心理学家、社会学家、神经学家和生育专家的知识

sentences.en: already know: that claiming your 20s is one of the simplest, yet most transformative, things you can do for work, for love, for your happiness, maybe even for the world.
sentences.zh: 我们已经知道：宣告自己的 20 多岁是最简单但最具变革性的事情之一，你可以为工作、爱情、幸福，甚至可能为世界做一些事情。

sentences.en: This is not my opinion. These are the facts.
sentences.zh: 这不是我的意见。这些都是事实。

sentences.en: We know that 80 percent of life's most defining moments take place by age 35.
sentences.zh: 我们知道，人生 80% 最具决定性的时刻发生在 35 岁之前。

sentences.en: That means that eight out of 10 of the decisions and experiences and "Aha!" moments that make your life what it is will have happened by your mid-30s.
sentences.zh: 这意味着十分之八的决定和经历都是“啊哈！”那些让你的生活变得美好的时刻将会在你 30 多岁的时候发生。

sentences.en: People who are over 40, don't panic. This crowd is going to be fine, I think.
sentences.zh: 40岁以上的人不要惊慌。我想这群人会没事的。

sentences.en: We know that the first 10 years of a career has an exponential impact on how much money you're going to earn.
sentences.zh: 我们知道，职业生涯的前 10 年会对您的收入产生指数级影响。

sentences.en: We know that more than half of Americans are married or are living with or dating their future partner by 30.
sentences.zh: 我们知道，超过一半的美国人在 30 岁时已结婚、与未来的伴侣同居或约会。

sentences.en: We know that the brain caps off its second and last growth spurt in your 20s as it rewires itself for adulthood, which means that whatever it is you want to change about yourself, now is the time to change it.
sentences.zh: 我们知道，大脑会在 20 多岁的时候结束第二次也是最后一次生长高峰，因为它会为成年而重新布线，这意味着无论你想改变自己的什么，现在就是改变它的时候了。

sentences.en: We know that personality changes more during your 20s than at any other time in life, and we know that female fertility peaks at age 28, and things get tricky after age 35.
sentences.zh: 我们知道，20 多岁时性格的变化比人生中任何其他时期都要大，而且女性的生育能力在 28 岁时达到顶峰，而 35 岁之后事情就会变得棘手。

sentences.en: So your 20s are the time to educate yourself about your body and your options.
sentences.zh: 因此，20 多岁是时候了解自己的身体和选择。

sentences.en: So when we think about child development, we all know that the first five years are a critical period for language and attachment in the brain.
sentences.zh: 因此，当我们考虑儿童发展时，我们都知道前五年是大脑中语言和依恋的关键时期。

sentences.en: It's a time when your ordinary, day-to-day life has an inordinate impact on who you will become.
sentences.zh: 在这个时期，你的日常生活会对你将成为什么样的人产生巨大的影响。

sentences.en: But what we hear less about is that there's such a thing as adult development, and our 20s are that critical period of adult development.
sentences.zh: 但我们很少听到的是，有成人发展这样的事情，而我们的20多岁正是成人发展的关键时期。

sentences.en: But this isn't what twentysomethings are hearing.
sentences.zh: 但这不是二十多岁的人听到的。

sentences.en: Newspapers talk about the changing timetable of adulthood.
sentences.zh: 报纸谈论成年期的变化时间表。

sentences.en: Researchers call the 20s an extended adolescence.
sentences.zh: 研究人员将 20 多岁称为延长的青春期。

sentences.en: Journalists coin silly nicknames for twentysomethings like "twixters" and "kidults."
sentences.zh: 记者们给二十多岁的年轻人起了一些愚蠢的绰号，比如“twixters”和“kidults”。

sentences.en: (Laughing) It's true! As a culture, we have trivialized what is actually the defining decade of adulthood.
sentences.zh: （笑）这是真的！作为一种文化，我们忽视了成年期的决定性十年。

sentences.en: Leonard Bernstein said that to achieve great things, you need a plan and not quite enough time.
sentences.zh: 伦纳德·伯恩斯坦（Leonard Bernstein）说过，要取得伟大的成就，你需要一个计划，但时间不够。

sentences.en: (Laughing) Isn't that true? So what do you think happens when you pat a twentysomething on the head and you say, "You have 10 extra years to start your life"?
sentences.zh: （笑）这不是真的吗？那么，当你拍拍一个二十多岁的人的头并说“你还有 10 年的时间来开始你的生活”时，你认为会发生什么？

sentences.en: Nothing happens. You have robbed that person of his urgency and ambition, and absolutely nothing happens.
sentences.zh: 什么也没发生。你剥夺了那个人的紧迫感和野心，绝对不会发生任何事情。

sentences.en: And then every day, smart, interesting twentysomethings like you or like your sons and daughters come into my office and say things like this: "I know my boyfriend's no good for me,
sentences.zh: 然后每天，像你或你的儿子和女儿一样聪明、有趣的二十多岁的人来到我的办公室，说这样的话：“我知道我的男朋友对我没有好处，

sentences.en: but this relationship doesn't count. I'm just killing time."
sentences.zh: 但这种关系不算数。我只是在消磨时间。”

sentences.en: Or they say, "Everybody says as long as I get started on a career by the time I'm 30, I'll be fine."
sentences.zh: 或者他们说，“每个人都说，只要我在 30 岁时开始工作，我就没事了。”

sentences.en: But then it starts to sound like this: "My 20s are almost over, and I have nothing to show for myself.
sentences.zh: 但后来听起来就像这样：“我的 20 多岁已经快结束了，我没有什么可以展示给自己的了。

sentences.en: I had a better résumé the day after I graduated from college."
sentences.zh: 大学毕业后的第二天，我就有了一份更好的简历。”

sentences.en: And then it starts to sound like this: "Dating in my 20s was like musical chairs.
sentences.zh: 然后它开始听起来像这样：“我 20 多岁的时候约会就像抢椅子。

sentences.en: Everybody was running around and having fun, but then sometime around 30 it was like the music turned off and everybody started sitting down.
sentences.zh: 每个人都跑来跑去，玩得很开心，但到了 30 岁左右的时候，音乐好像关掉了，每个人都开始坐下来。

sentences.en: I didn't want to be the only one left standing up, so sometimes I think I married my husband because he was the closest chair to me at 30."
sentences.zh: 我不想成为唯一一个站着的人，所以有时我想我嫁给了我的丈夫，因为他是我 30 岁时离我最近的椅子。”

sentences.en: Where are the twentysomethings here? Do not do that.
sentences.zh: 这里的二十多岁的人在哪里？不要那样做。

sentences.en: (Laughter) Okay, now that sounds a little flip, but make no mistake, the stakes are very high.
sentences.zh: （笑声） 好吧，这听起来有点反常，但毫无疑问，风险非常高。

sentences.en: When a lot has been pushed to your 30s, there is enormous thirtysomething pressure to jump-start a career, pick a city, partner up, and have two or three kids in a much shorter period of time.
sentences.zh: 当很多事情都被推到30多岁时，三十多岁的人就会面临巨大的压力，需要在更短的时间内开始职业生涯、选择城市、结婚、生两三个孩子。

sentences.en: Many of these things are incompatible, and as research is just starting to show, simply harder and more stressful to do all at once in our 30s.
sentences.zh: 其中许多事情是不相容的，正如研究刚刚开始表明的那样，在我们 30 多岁的时候一次性完成所有事情会更加困难和压力更大。

sentences.en: The post-millennial midlife crisis isn't buying a red sports car.
sentences.zh: 千禧一代后的中年危机不是购买红色跑车。

sentences.en: It's realizing you can't have that career you now want.
sentences.zh: 它是意识到你无法拥有你现在想要的职业。

sentences.en: It's realizing you can't have that child you now want, or you can't give your child a sibling.
sentences.zh: 它是意识到你不能拥有你现在想要的孩子，或者你不能给你的孩子一个兄弟姐妹。

sentences.en: Too many thirtysomethings and fortysomethings look at themselves, and at me, sitting across the room, and say about their 20s, "What was I doing? What was I thinking?"
sentences.zh: 太多的三十多岁和四十多岁的人看着自己，看着坐在房间另一边的我，然后说他们 20 多岁的时候，“我在做什么？我在想什么？”

sentences.en: I want to change what twentysomethings are doing and thinking.
sentences.zh: 我想改变二十多岁的人的行为和想法。

sentences.en: Here's a story about how that can go. It's a story about a woman named Emma.
sentences.zh: 这是一个关于如何进行的故事。这是一个关于一个名叫艾玛的女人的故事。

sentences.en: At 25, Emma came to my office because she was, in her words, having an identity crisis.
sentences.zh: 25 岁时，艾玛来到我的办公室，用她的话说，因为她遇到了身份危机。

sentences.en: She said she thought she might like to work in art or entertainment, but she hadn't decided yet, so she'd spent the last few years waiting tables instead.
sentences.zh: 她说她认为自己可能喜欢从事艺术或娱乐行业，但她还没有决定，所以过去几年她一直在当服务员。

sentences.en: Because it was cheaper, she lived with a boyfriend who displayed his temper more than his ambition.
sentences.zh: 因为便宜，她和一个脾气比野心还大的男朋友住在一起。

sentences.en: And as hard as her 20s were, her early life had been even harder.
sentences.zh: 尽管她二十多岁的时候过得很艰难，但她早年的生活更加艰难。

sentences.en: She often cried in our sessions, but then would collect herself by saying, "You can't pick your family, but you can pick your friends."
sentences.zh: 她经常在我们的治疗中哭泣，但随后会平静地说：“你不能选择你的家人，但你可以选择你的朋友。”

sentences.en: Well one day, Emma comes in and she hangs her head in her lap, and she sobbed for most of the hour.
sentences.zh: 有一天，艾玛进来了，她把头埋在腿上，哭了大半个小时。

sentences.en: She'd just bought a new address book, and she'd spent the morning filling in her many contacts, but then she'd been left staring at that empty blank that comes after the words "In case of emergency, please call ..."
sentences.zh: 她刚刚买了一本新的通讯录，花了一上午的时间填写了许多联系人信息，但随后她就只剩下盯着“如有紧急情况，请致电……”之后的空白。

sentences.en: She was nearly hysterical when she looked at me and said, "Who's going to be there for me if I get in a car wreck?
sentences.zh: 她几乎歇斯底里地看着我说：“如果我遭遇车祸，谁会在我身边？

sentences.en: Who's going to take care of me if I have cancer?"
sentences.zh: 如果我得了癌症谁来照顾我？”

sentences.en: Now in that moment, it took everything I had not to say, "I will."
sentences.zh: 在那一刻，我竭尽全力才没有说出“我会的”。

sentences.en: But what Emma needed wasn't some therapist who really, really cared.
sentences.zh: 但艾玛需要的并不是某个真正非常关心的治疗师。

sentences.en: Emma needed a better life, and I knew this was her chance.
sentences.zh: 艾玛需要更好的生活，我知道这是她的机会。

sentences.en: I had learned too much since I first worked with Alex to just sit there while Emma's defining decade went parading by.
sentences.zh: 自从第一次和亚历克斯一起工作以来，我学到了太多东西，不能只是坐在那里，看着艾玛决定性的十年过去。

sentences.en: So over the next weeks and months, I told Emma three things that every twentysomething, male or female, deserves to hear.
sentences.zh: 因此，在接下来的几周和几个月里，我告诉艾玛每一个二十多岁的人，无论男性还是女性，都应该听到三件事。

sentences.en: First, I told Emma to forget about having an identity crisis and get some identity capital.
sentences.zh: 首先，我告诉艾玛忘记身份危机并获得一些身份资本。

sentences.en: By "get identity capital," I mean do something that adds value to who you are.
sentences.zh: 我所说的“获得身份资本”是指做一些能为你自己增值的事情。

sentences.en: Do something that's an investment in who you might want to be next.
sentences.zh: 做一些对你可能想成为下一个人的人进行投资的事情。

sentences.en: I didn't know the future of Emma's career, and no one knows the future of work, but I do know this: Identity capital begets identity capital.
sentences.zh: 我不知道艾玛职业生涯的未来，也没有人知道工作的未来，但我确实知道这一点：身份资本产生身份资本。

sentences.en: So now is the time for that cross-country job, that internship, that startup you want to try.
sentences.zh: 所以现在是你想要尝试的跨国工作、实习、创业的时候了。

sentences.en: I'm not discounting twentysomething exploration here, but I am discounting exploration that's not supposed to count, which, by the way, is not exploration.
sentences.zh: 我在这里并不是贬低二十多岁的探索，而是贬低那些不应该算数的探索，顺便说一句，这不是探索。

sentences.en: That's procrastination. I told Emma to explore work and make it count.
sentences.zh: 这就是拖延症。我告诉艾玛要探索工作并让它发挥作用。

sentences.en: Second, I told Emma that the urban tribe is overrated.
sentences.zh: 其次，我告诉艾玛，城市部落被高估了。

sentences.en: Best friends are great for giving rides to the airport, but twentysomethings who huddle together with like-minded peers limit who they know, what they know, how they think, how they speak, and where they work.
sentences.zh: 最好的朋友很乐意搭车去机场，但二十多岁的年轻人与志同道合的同龄人挤在一起会限制他们认识的人、他们知道的事情、他们的想法、他们的说话方式以及他们的工作地点。

sentences.en: That new piece of capital, that new person to date almost always comes from outside the inner circle.
sentences.zh: 新的资本、新的约会对象几乎总是来自核心圈子之外。

sentences.en: New things come from what are called our weak ties, our friends of friends of friends.
sentences.zh: 新事物来自于我们所谓的弱联系，我们的朋友的朋友的朋友。

sentences.en: So yes, half of twentysomethings are un- or under-employed.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，二十多岁的人中有一半失业或就业不足。

sentences.en: But half aren't, and weak ties are how you get yourself into that group.
sentences.zh: 但有一半的人不是，弱关系是你进入这个群体的方式。

sentences.en: Half of new jobs are never posted, so reaching out to your neighbor's boss is how you get that unposted job.
sentences.zh: 一半的新职位从未发布过，因此联系邻居的老板是获得未发布职位的方法。

sentences.en: It's not cheating. It's the science of how information spreads.
sentences.zh: 这不是作弊。这是关于信息如何传播的科学。

sentences.en: Last but not least, Emma believed that you can't pick your family, but you can pick your friends.
sentences.zh: 最后但并非最不重要的一点是，艾玛相信你无法选择你的家人，但你可以选择你的朋友。

sentences.en: Now this was true for her growing up, but as a twentysomething, soon Emma would pick her family when she partnered with someone and created a family of her own.
sentences.zh: 在她的成长过程中确实如此，但作为一个二十多岁的人，当艾玛与某人合作并创建自己的家庭时，很快她就会选择她的家庭。

sentences.en: I told Emma the time to start picking your family is now.
sentences.zh: 我告诉艾玛现在是开始挑选你的家人的时候了。

sentences.en: Now you may be thinking that 30 is actually a better time to settle down than 20, or even 25, and I agree with you.
sentences.zh: 现在你可能会认为30岁实际上比20岁甚至25岁更适合安定下来，我同意你的观点。

sentences.en: But grabbing whoever you're living with or sleeping with when everyone on Facebook starts walking down the aisle is not progress.
sentences.zh: 但是，当 Facebook 上的每个人都开始走上红毯时，抓住与你同住或一起睡觉的人并不是进步。

sentences.en: The best time to work on your marriage is before you have one, and that means being as intentional with love as you are with work.
sentences.zh: 为婚姻而努力的最佳时机是在结婚之前，这意味着要像对待工作一样用心对待爱情。

sentences.en: Picking your family is about consciously choosing who and what you want rather than just making it work or killing time with whoever happens to be choosing you.
sentences.zh: 选择你的家人意味着有意识地选择你想要的人和你想要的东西，而不是仅仅让它发挥作用或与碰巧选择你的人一起消磨时间。

sentences.en: So what happened to Emma? Well, we went through that address book, and she found an old roommate's cousin who worked at an art museum in another state.
sentences.zh: 那么艾玛怎么了？好吧，我们查了那本地址簿，她找到了一位老室友的表弟，他在另一个州的一家艺术博物馆工作。

sentences.en: That weak tie helped her get a job there.
sentences.zh: 这条薄弱的领带帮助她在那里找到了工作。

sentences.en: That job offer gave her the reason to leave that live-in boyfriend.
sentences.zh: 这份工作给了她离开那个同居男友的理由。

sentences.en: Now, five years later, she's a special events planner for museums.
sentences.zh: 五年后的现在，她成为了博物馆的特别活动策划人。

sentences.en: She's married to a man she mindfully chose.
sentences.zh: 她嫁给了一个她精心选择的男人。

sentences.en: She loves her new career, she loves her new family, and she sent me a card that said, "Now the emergency contact blanks don't seem big enough."
sentences.zh: 她热爱她的新职业，她热爱她的新家庭，她给我寄了一张卡片，上面写着：“现在紧急联系人的空白似乎不够大。”

sentences.en: Now Emma's story made that sound easy, but that's what I love about working with twentysomethings.
sentences.zh: 艾玛的故事听起来很简单，但这就是我喜欢和二十多岁的人一起工作的原因。

sentences.en: They are so easy to help. Twentysomethings are like airplanes just leaving LAX, bound for somewhere west.
sentences.zh: 他们很容易提供帮助。二十多岁的人就像刚离开洛杉矶国际机场的飞机，飞往西部的某个地方。

sentences.en: Right after takeoff, a slight change in course is the difference between landing in Alaska or Fiji.
sentences.zh: 起飞后，航向的微小变化就是降落在阿拉斯加或斐济的区别。

sentences.en: Likewise, at 21 or 25 or even 29, one good conversation, one good break, one good TED Talk, can have an enormous effect across years and even generations to come.
sentences.zh: 同样，在 21 岁、25 岁甚至 29 岁时，一次愉快的谈话、一次愉快的休息、一次精彩的 TED 演讲，可以对未来数年甚至几代人产生巨大影响。

sentences.en: So here's an idea worth spreading to every twentysomething you know.
sentences.zh: 因此，这里有一个值得向您认识的每一位二十多岁的人传播的想法。

sentences.en: It's as simple as what I learned to say to Alex.
sentences.zh: 这就像我学会对亚历克斯说的话一样简单。

sentences.en: It's what I now have the privilege of saying to twentysomethings like Emma every single day: Thirty is not the new 20, so claim your adulthood, get some identity capital, use your weak ties,
sentences.zh: 这就是我现在有幸每天对像艾玛这样的二十多岁的人说的话：三十岁不是新的二十岁，所以宣告你的成年，获得一些身份资本，利用你的弱关系，

sentences.en: pick your family. Don't be defined by what you didn't know or didn't do.
sentences.zh: 选择你的家人。不要被你不知道或没有做过的事情所定义。

sentences.en: You're deciding your life right now. Thank you.
sentences.zh: 你现在正在决定你的生活。谢谢。

sentences.en: (Applause)
sentences.zh: （掌声）
